issues.description: signing_mode_enum is non-exhaustive: the (is_hex=False, safe_mode=True) case falls through to a bare default return.
issues.detail: Three of four (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations are handled explicitly; the fourth is satisfied only by the final unconditional return CHIP_0002. A reader must truth-table the function to prove correctness. Replace with an exhaustive match or a dict keyed by (is_hex, safe_mode) so the mapping is a single readable table.

issues.description: sign_message and verify_signature duplicate the SigningMode-to-message-bytes mapping.
issues.detail: Both functions reimplement the same mode dispatch that converts a message under a SigningMode into the bytes actually signed or verified. Extract one shared helper message_bytes(mode, message) -> bytes used by both, so the sign/verify invariant is textual rather than coincidental and the next CHIP mode is added in exactly one place.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is a stale stub referencing a request parameter that no longer exists.
issues.detail: The function now takes keyword args (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address) but the docstring still reads ':param request:' carried over from the RPC method. Documentation that misrepresents the signature is worse than none; rewrite it to describe the actual contract or remove the stub.

issues.description: verify_signature leaks the RPC VerifySignatureResponse type into the wallet util layer.
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports and returns VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types, coupling the util module to the RPC wire shape. The library contract should be a plain bool plus an error reason (or a small result struct local to signing.py) so non-RPC callers can reuse it, which is the stated motivation for the extraction.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is a Wallet instance method that uses no instance state.
issues.detail: The method only calls calculate_synthetic_secret_key with DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH and never reads self. Callers reach through self.service.wallet_state_manager.main_wallet just to invoke a pure value transform that has nothing to do with main_wallet identity. Move it to a module-level function in chia/wallet/util/signing.py (or make it staticmethod).

issues.description: Variable hex_message in sign_message holds non-hex bytes in three of four branches.
issues.detail: The local is named hex_message but is assigned UTF-8 bytes, a Program tree hash, and raw bytes depending on mode; only one branch actually involves hex. The name was inherited from the old wallet method. Rename to message_to_sign (mirroring verify_signature's message_to_verify) so the sign/verify symmetry is visible.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a structurally correct extraction: three near-duplicate sign_message implementations across Wallet, DIDWallet, and NFTWallet collapse into a single chia/wallet/util/signing.py module, and the wallets reduce to exposing a puzzle hash. The execution stops one step short of the cleanup that motivates the move. The new signing_mode_enum helper relies on a non-exhaustive fall-through, the SigningMode-to-bytes dispatch is duplicated between sign_message and verify_signature, the verify_signature docstring is stale, and the util module leaks the RPC VerifySignatureResponse type. Several smaller boundary issues remain (convert_secret_key_to_synthetic on Wallet uses no instance state, hex_message is a misleading name). Land after tightening the dispatch, docstring, and abstraction boundary.
